rationale: Mark 3:22-30 runs through the same sequence as Matthew 12:24-32: the charge of casting out demons by Beelzebul, the divided kingdom and house, the strong man, and the saying on blasphemy against the Holy Spirit. Some of the BSB wording is identical: "unless he first ties up the strong man" and "Then he can plunder his house" (Matthew 12:29; Mark 3:27), though the Greek word order differs. The same saying and the same order are why the type is parallel and the label strong; a synoptic parallel is graded parallel/strong, not explicit, as with conn-matt10-sword-luke12. The differences are checkable in the BSB and bear on the lesson's questions. In Mark the accusers are "the scribes who had come down from Jerusalem" (3:22), not "the Pharisees" (Matthew 12:24). Mark has "he is guilty of eternal sin" (3:29) where Matthew has "either in this age or in the one to come" (12:32). Mark alone adds the reason: "Jesus made this statement because they were saying, 'He has an unclean spirit'" (3:30), a verse several readers in the lesson use to fix what the sin is. Mark has no healing to open the scene and no "Son of David" question.
